title: n8n SSO Pricing: Which Plans Include It (2026)
summary: n8n SSO is unavailable in the Community edition. Check which paid tiers offer it and whether open-source alternatives like Activepieces include it.
body_markdown:
## Single sign-on in Activepieces for the same job


### Where Activepieces keeps SSO


Activepieces puts SSO in a Security page of its admin panel, with Google sign-in, SAML 2.0 and allowed email domains as separate switches. The edition question you just worked through still applies, but the protocol side is less to configure.


In the screenshot, Security is open in the left sidebar with "Single Sign On" selected, and the main panel lists four options: Allowed Domains, Google, SAML 2.0 and Allowed Email Login.


The first three each have an Enable button. Allowed Email Login is a toggle, and it's currently on.


Take two things from it. Google covers a team whose accounts already live in Google Workspace, so you don't need a SAML identity provider just to get single sign-on.


And the email toggle means password-style login stays open until you switch it off, so enabling SSO alone doesn't lock anyone out of the old route.


### Which edition unlocks it


The panel doesn't say which edition unlocks these settings, and I won't guess.


The pricing page lists Free at $0, Plus at $20 a month, Team at $200 a month and Ultimate through sales, so check Activepieces' SSO documentation against those four before you commit, using the same test as for n8n: your identity provider, your user count, your audit needs.


### n8n SSO licensing and free trial options


Licensing is simpler. The core is open source under the MIT licence, so you can self-host it without the usage restrictions that put some teams off n8n's Sustainable Use License.


The enterprise directories carry a separate commercial licence, while the core is MIT., including SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, release management and secret manager integration.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


There's also a free cloud plan that asks for no card, which lets you build a real workflow before anyone talks about budget.


Activepieces doesn't import or convert n8n workflows. You rebuild them, so check that the apps a workflow touches are among the 741 integrations in the open source monorepo, then try one small, annoying workflow first and judge the editor on that.


The free cloud plan at[activepieces.com](https://www.activepieces.com/) is $0 with 1,000 credits a month, unlimited flows and up to 5 users, and when the credits run out, flows wait for the next day's credits.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams that need the full enterprise feature set (SSO, SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, release management and secret managers) under their own control, judged on whether an air-gapped install gives up anything compared with the managed cloud.


The docs list the same features either way, so choosing self-hosting costs no capability, and the SSO page shows a plain setup with Google, SAML 2.0 and allowed domains as separate switches.


A team that prefers a managed, region-pinned service with SOC 2 Type II may still reasonably go to the cloud, but it would be choosing that for operational convenience and not because it gets more features.
